at 11.5a.m. on the 10/2/27 information was received at this
station to the effect that a Labour Union meeting was being held
in the premises of the Shanghai Electric Construction Company's
Employees Union, No. 338 Yulin Road; All available men at this

young women were holding a meeting in a large room on the upper

addressing the meeting, while the audience were all seated in
rows, on forms, facing the Speakers' table. On D.I. Prince
entering this room the speaker stopped his address, therefore
the subject of it could not be ascertained, but it was afterwards
learned, that the Speakers were bringing to the notice of the
audience the fact, that the employees of the Shanghai Tramway
Company, S.M.C. Electricity Department, Waterworks Department,
and other Foreign firms had induced, or forced, their employers to
increase their wages, and that now it was the duty of the members
of the various Labour Unions to urge the proprietors of large
Chinese Establishments to increase the wages of their employees,
where this had not already been done. On the appearance of the
Police at this meeting there was no disturbance. Inspector
Morgan then communicated with the Commissioner of Police by tele-
phone and Orders were received to arrest the leading persons at
the meeting, whereupon the speaker and his three confederates at

February 7th Anniversary.

Brief story of the February 7th incident.

February 7th is the day of commemoration of the shedding
of blood of the Peking-Hankow Railway workers who resisted
Wu Pei Fu(吳佩孚). It was on February 1 of 1923 when the
General Union of the Peking-Hankow Railway Workers held its
inaugural meeting in Chenchow that the cruel Wu Pei Fu suddenly
proclaimed Martial Law and oppressed the workers in every way
possible. The workers however were not daunted, and passed a
resolution at the meeting to call a general strike as a protest
against Wu Pei Fu's action. On February 7 when the workers had
already been on strike for four days, Wu Pei Fu ordered his
"Claws"(subordinates) to slaughter workers. Workers were also
murdered by Wu's men at places other than Chenchow. It is
calculated that 44 workers were killed and several hundred others
wounded. This was the first time that workers fought desperately
with the militarists.

February 7th was the day when workers commenced to struggle for
liberty.

Prior to February 7 the Chinese workers were not yet
awakened. On February 7 xxx workers began to struggle for the
right of organizing unions. Since then the workers have
organized more labour unions day after day. Although the workers
have now struggled for several years, labour unions can not be
publicly opened in many places. Therefore we must continue the
February 7th spirit and resist our enemies, the Imperialists and
Militarists.

February 7th is an important factor in the Revolutionary Movement.

The revolutionary spirit and strength of the labouring
classes was not recognized until the bloodshed on February 7.
Since then our countrymen recognize the labouring classes as
leaders in the Revolutionary movement. In the May 30th tragedy,

二月七周年纪念。

二月七日事件简述。

二月七日是纪念京汉铁路工人抵抗吴佩孚（吳佩孚）而流血的日子。1923年2月1日，京汉铁路工人总工会在郑州举行成立大会时，残酷的吴佩孚突然宣布戒严，并千方百计压迫工人。然而，工人们并未气馁，并在会上通过决议，号召举行总罢工以抗议吴佩孚的行径。2月7日，当工人们已经罢工四天时，吴佩孚命令他的“爪牙”（下属）屠杀工人。除郑州外，吴的手下也在其他地方杀害了工人。据估计，有44名工人被杀，数百人受伤。这是工人第一次与军阀进行殊死搏斗。

二月七日是工人开始争取自由的日子。

在二月七日之前，中国工人尚未觉醒。2月7日 xxx 工人开始为组织工会的权利而斗争。此后，工人日复一日地组织了更多的工会。虽然工人们现在已经斗争了几年，但在许多地方工会仍不能公开成立。因此，我们必须继续发扬二月七日精神，抵抗我们的敌人，即帝国主义者和军阀。

二月七日是革命运动的重要因素。

直到二月七日流血事件发生后，劳动阶级的革命精神和力量才得到认可。从此，我国同胞认识到劳动阶级是革命运动的领导者。在五卅惨案中，工人也发挥了领导作用。因此，工人应该再-

2.
double their efforts and continue to act as leaders in all
movements.
Advice to workers after the February 7th movement.
In the February 7th movement, a great number of
workers were killed, labour unions were closed, and numerous
persons were thrown out of employment. However, only one year
after February 7th, the National General Labour Union of Railway
Employees came into existence. Due to the efforts of workers
throughout the country to resist him, Wu Pei Fu will now soon
perish. Therefore, no matter how strong our enemies are, we
will overthrow them if every one of our workers will use his best
exertions. We must bear in mind that only by incessant
struggle can we win the final victory. We cannot avoid
temporary failures, and let us not be discouraged in anyway.
How to commemorate the February 7th Anniversary?
A worthwhile commemoration of the February 7
movement is that we should unite more closely and re-double our
efforts in the struggle. If on this particular occasion we
merely conduct a memorial meeting but fail to continue the
February 7th spirit and to struggle for our rights, it is not a
commemoration.
Our slogans are as the following:
Continue the Feb. 7 spirit!
Overthrow the brutal Wu Pei Fu!
Oppose the xx killing of our countrymen by Britishers in
Hankow!
Long live the spirits of the martyrs in the Feb. 7
movement!
A great day for workers is February 7!
Labourers constitute the vanguards of the revolutionary
forces!
( Chopped) The Shanghai General Labour
Union. 3/2/27.

2.
加倍努力，继续在所有运动中发挥领导作用。
二月七日运动后对工人的建议。
在二月七日运动中，大量工人被杀，工会被关闭，许多人失业。然而，在二月七日仅一年后，全国铁路员工总工会成立了。由于全国各地工人努力抵抗他，吴佩孚现在即将灭亡。因此，无论我们的敌人多么强大，如果我们每一位工人都竭尽全力，我们就将推翻他们。我们必须牢记，只有不断的斗争才能赢得最终胜利。我们无法避免暂时的失败，让我们不要以任何方式气馁。
如何纪念二月七周年？
对二月七日运动有价值的纪念方式是，我们应该更紧密地团结起来，在斗争中加倍努力。如果在这个特定场合，我们仅仅举行追悼会，而不能继续发扬二月七日精神并为我们的权利而斗争，那就不是纪念。
我们的口号如下：
继续发扬二月七日精神！
推翻残暴的吴佩孚！
反对英国人在汉口 xx 杀害我们的同胞！
二月七日运动中烈士精神万岁！
二月七日是工人的伟大日子！
劳动者构成革命力量的先锋！
（盖章）上海总工会。1927年2月3日。

----------

工会是工人的堡垒。所有工人都应组织工会并加入其中。

2月7日是工人开始开展国民革命运动的日子。这证明中国工人是国民革命的先锋。起来！起来！让我们团结起来，奋勇前进！

will never die

tens of workers including one named S Yang (施洋)

the spirit which animated the men who died on
February 7!

Maintain the spirit of February 7

February 7 is the anniversary of the first battle waged
by the Chinese workers against the most wicked
militarists when the former shed their blood.
February 7 marks the commencement of the Revolution
in China. "Feb. 7" has awakened the Chinese
labourers from their dream. "Feb. 7" is indeed
a great day ! Let us continue our advance with
the same spirit that inspired on "February 7!"

Denounce the British Imperialists for Hankow
Slaughter

The robber-like British Imperialists have again killed
our brethren at Hankow. Get united, all you workers
in Shanghai and oppose the murderous British
Imperialists !

On January 19 the written proposals to certain

strikers, who promised to convey the said proposals to a

called at the residence of Mr. Yu Yah Ching, ex-Chairman of the

on behalf of the strikers. Yu Yah Ching on the same
evening interviewed Mr. Burgess and at the end of the
consultation definitely promised that the men had accepted
the proposals and would resume work on the morning of January 21.

Chief Cashier of the said company and the deputation of eight
where the terms of settlement; i.e. the proposals drawn up by
Mr. Burgess with a few minor alterations, were signed and

Commissioner of Police Barrett,

Foochow Road.

Sir,

After we and the Company signed the conditions for
the resumption of duty today, we decided to run some tram cars
through the different roads as an expression of resumption
of duty. When these tram cars came to the vicinity of
Pau Chiu Tsang (corner of Nanking and Honan Roads), the
electric current suddenly stopped with the result that
those cars could not proceed any longer, and the armed
policemen of your Station attacked us without a reasonable
cause resulting in several tens of our workers being
wounded and arrested. In the interests of peace we
restrained ourselves from beginning to the end and at
once repaired to our homes. The Company and the Police
are responsible for this unfortunate incident.

Apart from requesting the Tramway Company to compensate
the wounded and to communicate with you with a view to
effecting the release of those workers arrested as a
condition for the resumption of duty, we have to write
this for your information in the hope that you will
set the workers arrested free, so that communication may
be restored at an early date and the ill feeling of our
countrymen against the Police may not be enhanced.

Commissioner of Police,
Municipal Council.

Sir,
    We thank you heartily for the protection you have afforded us during our present strike which has lasted several days and we can assure you that no disorderly and improper deeds will be attempted.
    Our negotiations with the management of the Co. have come to a stand still on account of the elusive manner of the management who do not give the workers' delegates the least chance to set forth their grievances and who have practically refused all the demands submitted by the workers except the one for an increase of pay, even in the latter case only $1.00 (to each man) being agreed to, and rejected mediators. It is, however, to be noted that the longer the strike lasts the greater will be the loses and inconvenience that the workers and the community will sustain. It is therefore sincerely hoped that you will take our privations into consideration by requesting the management of the company to resume negotiations without delay with the workers' delegates, for the workers have no desire to prolong the strike inasmuch as their demands can be satisfactorily met with.

The Strike Committee of the Workers' Union of the Tramway Co. of the International Settlement.

Manifesto on Resumption of Work

Being unable to maintain our livelihood and
endure unreasonable oppression, we, all workers of the
Shanghai Electric Construction Co., struck work.
Despite the fact that we have twice entered into
negotiations with the Company, no satisfactory reply
has, so far, been received to our demand. In view
of much inconvenience experienced by the public, we,
although our objects have not been fully attained,
are willing to make concessions in order that the
service may be resumed at an early date. We have
therefore, signed an agreement with the Company, and
returned to our duties. We should, however, bear in
mind that we won this dispute only because we have
organized a labour union. Consequently we advocate
that labour unions should partake in any labour movement
and thereby seek means to strengthen the labour cause.
Thus victory will always be ours. We also feel
grateful for the mediation of Mr. Yu Ya Ching
(虞洽卿) and assistance rendered by the various labour
unions. We should realize that labour unions, when
and only when supported by all workers and helped by
brethren of various circles will gain their victories.

Shanghai Settlement Tramway
Employees' Labour Union,
22/1/27

由于无法维持生计且难以忍受不合理的压迫，我们上海电气建设公司的全体工人举行了罢工。尽管我们已与公司进行了两次谈判，但迄今为止，我们的要求尚未得到令人满意的答复。鉴于给公众带来诸多不便，虽然我们的目标尚未完全实现，但我们愿意做出让步，以便尽早恢复服务。因此，我们已与公司签署协议，并返回工作岗位。然而，我们要铭记，我们之所以赢得这场纠纷，仅仅是因为我们组织了工会。因此，我们主张工会应参与任何劳工运动，从而寻求加强劳工事业的方法。这样，胜利将永远属于我们。我们也感谢虞洽卿 (Yu Ya Ching) 先生的调解以及各工会提供的援助。我们应该认识到，工会只有在得到全体工人的支持并得到各界同胞的帮助时，才能取得胜利。

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Zung Yuen Pao, 29,
native of Hupeh taken by me D.S. Telfer
at 3 p.m. on the Jan. 23, 1927 and interpreted by Interpreter Kung

About 11 a.m. on Jan. 23, 1927, the bus No.31,
of which I am driver, left the St. Georges. When I was
proceeding West to East along Yangtszepoo Road, near the
Whashing Road, about 10 men of the coolie type, possibly in
the employ of the Tramway Co., lined across the roadway and
shouted to me to stop. As soon as I drew up the bus, about
4 men came up and caught hold of my woollen scarf and dragged
me off the bus. They then struck me with fists, caught hold
of my arms and forced me to go with them along Whashing Road.
They took me to a house No.204 Pingliang Road, where I saw
about 30 or 40 men, consisting of omnibus and tramway employees.
I was told to sit down and then about 5 men asked me if I knew
that there was a strike amongst the omnibus drivers. I told
them that I drove the bus by order of the Company, whereupon
they told me that if I was again seen driving a bus, I would
be assaulted. I asked them if they would allow me to go,
but they told me to wait. After 1½ hours later, Policemen
came to the place and asked me what had happened. I, accom-
panied by Police, then returned to Yangtszepoo and Whashing
Roads, where I found the window glass of the bus had been
smashed. I then drove the bus to the Police Station.

(Sd) Zung Yuen Pao

1927年1月23日上午约11时，我驾驶的31路公共汽车离开圣乔治大厦（St. Georges）。当我沿杨树浦路由西向东行驶，近华盛路（Whashing Road，原文如此，疑为Huashan Rd.或类似路名之误拼，此处照录）附近时，约十名苦力模样的人（可能是电车公司雇员）横挡在路中间，喝令我停车。我刚一停下车，约四名男子上前抓住我的羊毛围巾，将我拖下车。随后他们用拳头殴打我，抓住我的手臂，强迫我沿华盛路随他们前行。他们将我带到平凉路204号的一所房屋内，我看到那里约有三十至四十人，包括公共汽车和电车雇员。他们让我坐下，随后约五名男子问我是否知道公共汽车司机正在罢工。我告诉他们我是奉公司命令驾驶公共汽车，于是他们告诉我，如果再次看到我驾驶公共汽车，就会遭到殴打。我问他们是否允许我离开，但他们让我等待。一个半小时后，警察来到该处并询问发生了什么事。随后我在警察陪同下返回杨树浦路和华盛路，发现公共汽车的车窗玻璃已被砸碎。随后我将公共汽车开往警察局。

（签名）陈元保

I am omnibus conductor No. 57. About 1 p.m.
on Jan. 23, 1927, when the bus was proceeding West to East
along Yangtszepoo Road, near "hashing Road, I saw a crowd of
coolies, in the employ of the Tramway Co. standing on Yang-
tszepoo Road. They started to throw stones at the bus
whereupon all the passengers became afraid and left the bus.
I also got off the bus, but was immediately set upon by about
20 men, who threw me on the roadway and struck me with fists.
They attempted to force me to go with them along "hashing Road,
but I managed to escape from them. During the fight,
I lost a quantity of coppers and tickets. I then called a
ricsha and travelled to wayside where I made a report to
a route inspector.

Hwo Yu Ching

REPORT ON Strike Situation in Wayside District.
Made by J. W. Prince D. I. Forwarded by T. Carndale C/I
Sir,
I beg to report that the Shanghai Ominbus Company's Buses resumed running, as usual, in this District this morning, but were withdrawn from the streets again at 2p.m. owing to inter-ference by strike agitators, and after one of the Buses plying on Yangtszepoo Road had been attacked and damaged by strike agitators.
At 6a.m. today three tramcars, for No. 7 Route, left the Yangtszepoo Road Depot, to resume running, but these cars were only brought as far as the corner of Broadway and Muirhead Road, when the drivers took them back to the Depot again. Their reason for doing so being, that they had been informed that if they proceeded further, loafers were going to attack and break up the cars. Three cars to run in 8 and 9 Routes were also taken out of the Depot at 6a.m. today but they only went as far as Broad-way Bridge, and then returned to the Depot, the drivers giving the same excuse for returning the cars as the others herein afore-mentioned.

The strike in the Shanghai Electric Construction Co.,

maintain the service during these days be given
double pay.
5. That wages be paid as usual to all workers for the
period of the strike.
6. That all new employees be engaged through the Employees'
Union.
7. That five ex-employees of the Company who lost their jobs
as a result of the General Strike on May 30, last year, be
re-instated.
8. That all increases in wages be paid in dollars and
fractions of dollars.
9. That half-day holiday be granted on the Dragon Boat
Festival, Mid-Autumn Festival and October 10, and that
double pay be issued to those who are called upon to
work on these occasions.
10. That no workers be dismissed for having participated

Sir,
I beg to report that at about 5 p.m. on the 22nd, January,
1927, employees of the Shanghai Electrical Construction Company
who are at present on strike, in all numbering about 1,500, start-
-ing off from Wayside Tramway Depot with the supposed intention
of conveying to the general public their intention of commencing
work on the 23rd, inst.. With the permission of the Tramway Coy.,
they used about fifteen tramcars & trailers to convey the process-
-ion from the above mentioned depot to Bubbling Well depot and
intended returning to Wayside. Their route was to be Broadway,
Nanking, & Bubbling Well Roads.
Under the belief that the procession of tramcars would go
through the International Settlement in quite an orderly & peace-
-ful manner & nothing demonstrative would be displayed ; police on
duty allowed them to traverse Wayside district. Immediately the
procession of tramcars left the view of the Wayside police the
strikers in the trams were reinforced by various union agitators,
when slogan banners were unfurled and, with addition of a plent-
-iful supply of crackers, the supposed orderly procession had all
appearance of turning into an agitated & disorderly demonstration.
At this point about twenty women were made use of by the strik-
-ers to shout various strike slogans & for general agitation
purposes.
This state of affairs continued until they reached the
Garden Bridge where the strikers gave renewed energy to their
vocal strike cries while the display of flags was noticeably
increased.

谨此报告，1927年1月22日下午5时许，目前正处于罢工状态的上海电气建设公司（Shanghai Electrical Construction Company）雇员，总数约1,500人，从韦斯特利（Wayside）电车车厂出发，据称意图向公众传达他们将于本月23日复工的决定。经电车公司许可，他们使用了约十五辆电车及拖车，将游行队伍从上述车厂运送至静安寺（Bubbling Well）车厂，并计划返回韦斯特利。其预定路线为百老汇路（Broadway）、南京路及静安寺路。

基于电车游行队伍将以相当有序且和平的方式穿过公共租界，且不会展示任何示威性物品的信念，执勤警察允许其穿过韦斯特利辖区。然而，电车游行队伍刚一离开韦斯特利警方的视线，电车上的罢工者便得到了各类工会煽动者的增援，此时展开了标语横幅，加之大量燃放鞭炮，原本所谓的有序游行完全呈现出转变为激动且混乱的示威活动的迹象。在此阶段，约二十名妇女被罢工者利用来高呼各种罢工口号并进行一般性的煽动活动。

此种状况一直持续至他们抵达外白渡桥（Garden Bridge），在那里，罢工者再次加大了口头罢工呐喊的力度，同时旗帜的展示明显增加。

reported the incident, after which they made a further report of it

Officers to the meeting place to make inquiries with reference to

not to go near the meeting lest any further disturbance should
arise, whereupon they went away again. At the conclusion of the
meeting the Chinese all formed into a procession and proceeded to
the Tramway Depot on Yangtsepoo Road with the presumed intention of
resuming work. A number of Car-drivers requested permission to
take their cars out, and when this was granted, and the cars were
taken out onto the road they were immediately filled by the people
who had been at the meeting. Altogether 10 cars with trailers

The strike in the Shanghai Electric Construction
Company, affecting 462 artisans of miscellaneous trades,
600 motormen, and 700 conductors, which started at 12 noon,
January 17, 1927 still continues. The strikers are still
using No. 204 Zung Woo Li (        ), corner of Pingliang
and Aushing Roads, as their offices. Letters purporting
to emanate from the Postal Employees' Union, No. 41 Shou Ying
Fong (        ) Ten Dung Road, near Dixwell Road, O.C.L.,
the Chinese Relief Society, No. 3 Sun Teh Li (        )
Paoshan Road, and containing promises that these
organizations will support the strikers are displayed
inside the premises. It is reported that the strikers are
planning to hold a general meeting at about 2 p.m.
to-day, January 20, 1927, near the corner of Thorburn
and Baikal Roads. The following letter from the Strikers'
Union was sent to the Yangtszepoo Station about 2.30 p.m.
January 19:-

    "To Inspector i-c Yangtszepoo Station:
    "We, tramway employees, went on strike with a
    "view to inducing the management to assist in
    "improving our livelihood, and our demands are
    "entirely of an economic nature. We ████ are
    "all prepared to resume work as soon as these
    "demands are granted. We are endeavouring to
    "preserve the peace and hope you will intervene
    "on our behalf and afford us protection. We
    "are sending a representative to see you with a

Sir,
I beg to report that at 6.25a.m. on the 18/1/'27 a
report was received at this station to the effect that certain
Tramway Company's employees, Fitters, were breaking up tram cars
on the Yangtsepoo Road, near Jansen Road. C. I. Crookdake, and

proceeding to the scene found that four tramcars running on the

three of the cars, with iron bars, after which they decamped
through alleyways. When the Police arrived on the scene, the men
who had damaged the cars had all disappeared, and inquiries, by
our men failed to discover their identity. Following this, the
damaged cars were all returned to the Yangtsepoo Road Depot, by
their Drivers, and from that time all Motormen, and Conductors,
and other employees at the above Depot have been on strike.

their employers, with reference to the strike among the Fitters

their employers in connection with their Service.

The following is a translation of a handbill giving
the demands of the employees of the Tramway Company on
strike, which was found in possession of two boys arrested
in Pukling well District on the morning of January 14, 1927:
Fellow workers,
We, the employees of the Shanghai Tramway Company, realize
that our living conditions are oppressive and intolerable.
At a general meeting of representatives of the whole body
of workers of the Mechanical and Traffic Departments, we
decided upon 17 demands which we have formally submitted
to the management of the company. As our demands have been
ignored, we and our colleagues in the Mechanical Department
have declared a strike. Representatives of the company have
announced that they will give us a definite reply next
Saturday. The foreigner named "Hunt", who is guilty of
assault, is willing to offer us an apology.
Fellow labourers !
We must pay special attention to the company's reply.
Let us conserve our strength and strive to attain our ends.
Our General Demands are :-
1. That the employees' wages be increased every year.
2. That employees be given one month's pay as a bonus at the
end of every Chinese year.
3. That the union of workers be recognized.
4. That foreigners be not allowed to insult or assault
workers; and that no workers be dismissed without the
consent of the labour union.
5. That employees be given five days' holiday at the Chinese
New Year without suffering loss of pay, and that employees
who consent to carry on the work during that period be given
double pay.
6. That employees be given full pay when they are on sick leave.

January 14th. 1927.

REPORT ON Shanghai Electric Construction Company's Employees.

Made by J. W. Prince D. I. Forwarded by P. Carless S/I

Sir,

I beg to report that about 400 Fitters, employed at
the Shanghai Electric Construction Company's Depot in the Eastern
District, stopped work on the 13/1/'27 pending settlement of
certain demands, which the men had laid before their employers.
These men all returned to work at 1.30p.m. on 14/1/'27, after
they had been informed that the Management would lay their demands
before the Company's Directors, whose decision would be made known
to the men after a week's time.

D. C. I.

I am, Sir,
Yours Obediently,
J.W. Prince
D. I.

关于上海电气建设公司员工的报告。

由警探普林斯（J. W. Prince）撰写，经副督察卡利斯（P. Carless）转呈

先生，

谨此报告，约400名受雇于东区上海电气建设公司车厂的装配工，于1927年1月13日停工，以待解决他们向雇主提出的某些要求。在获知管理层将把他们的要求提交给公司董事，且董事的决定将在一周后告知员工后，这些人均于1927年1月14日下午1时30分复工。

副总督察。
